description.value: The study examined age-related changes in visual word perception, resting-state functional connectivity within the word-selective network and between that network and other brain regions, and the relationship between connectivity changes and visual word-matching performance.

design.value: The study recruited healthy older and young adults and first collected resting-state fMRI data, followed by a block-designed word localizer task during task fMRI. Word-selective left and right ventral occipitotemporal regions were identified from group-level localizer activation maps and used as seeds for resting-state functional connectivity analyses. Participants subsequently completed word-matching and symbol-form matching behavioral tasks.

description.value: The Chinese version of the Combined Raven’s Test, published in 1991, was used to evaluate non-verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) and general cognitive ability.

Participants judged whether two visually presented words were identical and pressed the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible. Inverse efficiency score was calculated as the average correct reaction time divided by the proportion of correct responses.

A baseline control test using symbol forms followed the same procedure as the word matching test. Inverse efficiency score was calculated as the average correct reaction time divided by the proportion of correct responses.

description.value: 19 healthy older adults; 11 men. All participants were right-handed individuals with no history of encephalopathy or mental illness, exhibited normal vision, and were instructed to rest adequately the day before the experiment.

description.value: 22 young adults; 11 men. All participants were right-handed individuals with no history of encephalopathy or mental illness, exhibited normal vision, and were instructed to rest adequately the day before the experiment. Due to procedural and recording issues, data from three participants in the young adult group were missing for the behavioral tasks.

exclusion_criteria.value: no history of encephalopathy or mental illness

task_description.value: This study first collected resting-state fMRI data from all participants in a quiet state.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to keep their heads as still as possible during the scan.

task_description.value: After acquiring the rs-fMRI data, participants performed a localizer task that involved a simple location judgment task. Visual stimuli were divided into two types: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters. The task included 16 blocks of visual stimulation and 16 blocks of fixation (“+”), each lasting 15 s in a balanced order. Each picture was presented for 250 ms, followed by a 750-ms inter-stimulus interval. Stimuli were presented on either the left or right side of the fixation point, and participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

instructions.value: Participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters, presented on either the left or right side of a fixation point.

task_description.value: After completing all MRI scans, participants rested before performing a visual matching task in another room. The task included 30 new pictures of words in stick figure style. In each trial, a fixed fixation point “+” was presented at the center of the screen for 800 ms. Then, two words appeared for 200 ms, after which a gray blank screen was displayed. The trial proceeded to the next one after the participant pressed a button. The maximum duration of each trial was 5,000 ms. The test consisted of 60 trials, with randomized stimuli and same/different trials.

instructions.value: Participants must quickly determine whether the two words on the screen are identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 30 new pictures of words, all in stick figure style; the stimuli were black against the background, and the visual angle of each stimulus was 1.1.

task_description.value: A baseline control test using symbol-form matching was used to control for general cognitive aging effects, following the same procedure as the word matching test. It included 30 new pictures of symbols in stick figure style and formed part of the 60-trial visual matching test.

instructions.value: Participants must quickly determine whether the two symbols on the screen are identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 30 new pictures of symbols, all in stick figure style; the stimuli were black against the background, and the visual angle of each stimulus was 1.1.

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain the rs-fMRI data. The imaging parameters were 43 axial slices, TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, voxel size = 3.4 mm × 3.4 mm × 3.2 mm, flip angle = 90°, field of view = 220 × 220 mm², and matrix size = 64 × 64. The resting session comprised 240 contiguous volumes and lasted 8 min.

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain task-fMRI data. The imaging parameters were 43 axial slices, TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, voxel size = 3.4 mm × 3.4 mm × 3.2 mm, flip angle = 90°, field of view = 220 × 220 mm², and matrix size = 64 × 64. The task (localizer) session lasted 8 min and 10 s, resulting in a continuous time course of 245 time points.
Task-fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit. The preprocessing steps were identical to those in the previous study.

model_settings.value: The phase-scattered Chinese characters were used as a baseline in the localizer task, and activation levels caused by Chinese character images were compared. The linear contrast image was Chinese characters vs. scattered Chinese characters.
A one-sample t-test was performed to obtain the group-level activation map. The most activated voxels within the left and right vOT of each AAL region were selected at FDR correction, q < 0.05.

For within-network connectivity, Pearson correlation was calculated between the averaged time courses of the two vOT ROIs. For connectivity beyond the word network, Pearson correlations were computed between the averaged time course of each ROI and the time course of every voxel in the brain. Correlation coefficients were transformed to z-values using Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient with Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

model_settings.value: Two-sample t-tests compared connectivity values between older and young adult groups. For connectivity beyond the word network, analyses were performed within the AAL mask, with gender included as a covariate. Gaussian Random Field theory was applied for multiple-comparison correction, with p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level; tests were two-tailed.
Age was the between-subject variable, with older adults and young adults, and stimulus type was the within-subject variable, with word pictures and symbol pictures.
An independent-sample t-test compared the difference in IES between word and symbol processing.

A Pearson correlation coefficient was calculated between the mean connectivity value of each cluster showing significant between-group differences and the IES from the word-matching task. Correlation analyses used p < 0.05.

Partial correlations were computed between connectivity value in each cluster and the IES from the word-matching task, controlling for the IES from the symbol-form matching task. These analyses used p < 0.05.
